newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian linear bonds seen in holding pattern.
newsitem.headline: Belgian linear bonds seen in holding pattern.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which held onto light gains in line with Bunds in morning trading on Thursday, are expected to remain in a tight holding pattern for the rest of the week, traders said.
"It is very quiet all along the yield curve. There is hardly any activity," one trader said, adding that what business there was seemed restricted to dealers shuffling their positions.
"There is little domestic interest and no foreigners," he said.
Traders said there were occasional comments about the child sex, sleaze and murder scandals in the country, but no impact.
Traders said everyone was waiting for the U.S. August Producer Price Index due at 1230 GMT on Thursday, and the Consumer Price Index due at the same time on Friday.
The PPI figures are seen up 0.1 percent month-on-month and up 2.8 percent year-on-year. The CPI figures are seen flat month-on-month, and up 1.3 percent year-on-year.

Traders said the markets were waiting to see what kind of magic the government could perform to massage the national budget into shape ready for the European Union's single currency due to start in 1999. The government has to find savings of at least 100 billion francs for the 1997 budget.
The benchmark 2006 OLO yielded 6.51 percent, down from Wednesday's 6.55. The premium over Bunds narrowed two basis points to 22.
The frontmonth futures contract was 15 basis points up at 117.39, in a 117.39/117.29 range.
